Real OpenTelemetry Collector otlphttp requests
==============================================

Captured 2026-10-05 from a local Collector run once with Docker for this purpose, then
stopped and removed. All data is the synthetic demo data shipped with this project
(example.com, documentation IP ranges).

Version
-------
otelcol-contrib 0.161.0 (linux/arm64 on Apple Silicon, Docker Desktop 20.10.14 engine).
Image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib
  multi-arch index digest sha256:fd328de2552466ad78385e1b1289c3f2402b1c45f265b252aab1955b42845ac1
  (the "latest" tag on that date, resolved with docker buildx imagetools inspect).

Setup (scripts/capture_collector/ holds the config and the recorder)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
  python3 scripts/capture_collector/record.py OUT_DIR        # listens on :18080
  docker run -d --name collector-capture -p 4318:4318 \
    -v "$PWD/scripts/capture_collector/collector.yaml:/etc/otelcol-contrib/config.yaml:ro" \
    otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib@sha256:fd328de2552466ad78385e1b1289c3f2402b1c45f265b252aab1955b42845ac1
The Collector reaches the recorder through host.docker.internal:18080.

collector.yaml: otlp receiver (HTTP, port 4318) -> batch processor (timeout 1s) -> two
exporters, neither setting compression, so both use the default (gzip):
  otlphttp/json   traces_endpoint http://host.docker.internal:18080/json/v1/traces,
                  encoding json, header "Authorization: Bearer capture-not-a-secret"
                  (a dummy value; record.py stores authorization headers redacted)
  otlphttp/proto  traces_endpoint http://host.docker.internal:18080/proto/v1/traces,
                  default encoding (protobuf)

Sending
-------
One line (one OTLP JSON document) was taken from each demo trace file in
src/detecttrace/demo_data/traces/ (the first line of each) and posted with
  curl -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @line.json http://localhost:4318/v1/traces
Line A (traces-2026-08-18T00-57-52.000.jsonl.gz) was posted alone; 4 seconds later lines
B (traces-2026-09-03T09-30-00.000.jsonl.gz) and C (traces.jsonl.gz) were posted back to
back. All three answered 200. A has 68 spans, B 64, C 62.

Requests (bodies saved byte-for-byte, still compressed as sent; *.headers.json holds the
method, path and headers, with the authorization value redacted by record.py)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  json_gzip_1.body      POST /json/v1/traces  Content-Encoding gzip  5384 bytes
                        decompresses to 52450 bytes: line A as one resourceSpans entry
                        (68 spans)
  json_gzip_2.body      POST /json/v1/traces  Content-Encoding gzip  9115 bytes
                        decompresses to 97583 bytes: lines B and C merged into one
                        request (2 resourceSpans entries, 126 spans)
  protobuf_gzip_1.body  POST /proto/v1/traces  Content-Type application/x-protobuf,
                        Content-Encoding gzip  5702 bytes; the protobuf twin of
                        json_gzip_1 (use it for the unsupported-media-type test)
The recorder answered every request 200 with body {} and Content-Type application/json.

Sanitization
------------
None needed. The decompressed bodies were searched for IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, domain
names and e-mail addresses: only 192.0.2.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24 and 203.0.113.0/24
addresses, example.com hosts and userNNNN@example.com addresses occur. Files were
renamed, never edited.
